cls.quote: Five riding modes deliver the speed and power to own the road as a Class 1, 2, or 3 eBike.* New simplified labels, including Eco, Tour, Sport, Sport+, & Turbo, allow riders to choose their riding experience. ⟶ Thumb Throttle
cls.basis: maker says Class 1, 2, or 3 (selectable) with a throttle; ships as Class 2 (20 mph) per the maker FAQ; the listed 28 mph top speed is the unlocked Class 3 setting

cls.quote: All Lectric eBikes ship as a class 2 electric bike, meaning it has a throttle capable of propelling the bike at speeds of up to 20mph. Pedal assist will also be limited to 12 or 20mph in this setting depending on the model.
cls.basis: maker FAQ 'What is the classification of Lectric eBikes?'; the same answer says the XP, XPedition, XPeak, XPress, and XPress Lite can be unlocked to class 3 (28 mph)

cls.quote: The XP4 ships as a Class 2 eBike but flips to Class 3 with a few taps on the 3.5″ color display. The 500W rear hub motor, peaking at 1,092W with 55Nm torque, uses a torque sensor for smooth, natural pedaling. It’s quiet—some whine at full throttle, but it fades quickly. The motor confidently tackles flats and moderate hills, but steep climbs slow it to a crawl. The 750W version’s 85Nm torque might be the move for hilly spots.
cls.basis: review says it ships as Class 2 and can be switched to Class 3

tq.quote: A 500W rear hub motor (1092W peak) with 55Nm of torque supplies power and speed quicker than ever before. Stealth M24 technology delivers a quieter motor experience without sacrificing power. ⟶ Battery

wh.quote: 1092W of peak power combined with our Stealth M24 technology delivers a quiet motor that's built for the long haul with a 48V, 10.4Ah (500Wh) lithium-ion battery certified to UL 2271. The XP4 is also certified to UL 2849. ⟶ Fun That’s Easy to See

range.quote: The 48V, 10.4Ah (499Wh) battery, UL 2271-certified, powers up to 50 miles (I hit 44 miles—see Range section). The $200 17.5Ah (840Wh) Long-Range battery claims 85 miles, ideal for big rides. My test bike’s optional 5A charger filled the 10.4Ah battery in 2.5 hours.
range.basis: same page also says 'Estimated Range (from Lectric): 55 Miles'; reviewer's test 44 miles
